newsitem.title: GERMANY: German supreme court blocks Bavarian abortion law.
newsitem.headline: German supreme court blocks Bavarian abortion law.

text.p: Germany's highest court on Tuesday blocked a move by the state of Bavaria to limit the amount doctors can earn from carrying out abortions.

Judges at the Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe ruled substantial parts of a Bavarian law on abortion could not come into force on July 1 as planned while they conducted a full examination of its implications.

The law drafted by the conservative southern state stipulates that doctors earn no more than one quarter of their incomes from abortions and that only specially-licensed gynaecologists could perform a termination on outpatients.

Two doctors, whose clinics carry out around two thirds of all abortions registered in Bavaria, had complained to the court that the new law would leave them financially ruined and infringed on their freedom to carry out their work.
The court ruled it was better to block the measures for now rather than let them come into force as planned and then have to withdraw them if they were found to violate the constitution.

Bavaria's ruling Christian Social Union (CSU), an arch-conservative party with close links to the Roman Catholic Church, introduced the bill as a reaction to a 1995 national law governing abortion which it viewed as too liberal.
The judges are not expected to reach a definitive decision on the Bavarian bill until the end of the year at the earliest.
